title: Synthesizing superoscillations with just two frequencies
abstract: Superoscillations, band-limited signals that locally oscillate faster than their highest Fourier component, have recently enabled superspectroscopy and super-sensing. Previous experiments [Phys. Rev. Lett. 131, 153803 (2023), https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.131.153803 and APL Photonics 10, 086107 (2025), https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0271556] relied on combining four quasi-sinusoidal harmonics to generate temporal superoscillations. Here, we show that just two harmonics are sufficient to produce superoscillations of comparable quality, as quantified by the local frequency. By reanalyzing prior experimental data with two harmonics (0.5 and 0.6 THz) and performing new experiments with 0.9 and 1 THz harmonics, we demonstrate a twofold enhancement in local frequency relative to the highest frequency component -- matching the enhancement previously achieved with four harmonics. We provide a simple analytical explanation for the bichromatic superoscillations based on near-complete destructive interference, and identify an optimal frequency separation of approximately 10% that balances the superoscillatory frequency enhancement against signal amplitude. This simplification substantially lowers the experimental barrier to implementing superoscillation-based technology.
summary: This paper shows that generating superoscillations, which exhibit local frequencies exceeding the signal's highest Fourier component, can be achieved using only two constituent frequencies instead of the previously required four. By providing both analytical explanations and confirming results with new THz experiments, the authors significantly lower the experimental hurdle for developing superoscillation-based technologies.
main_problem: The primary goal is to synthesize superoscillations—band-limited signals that oscillate faster than their highest Fourier component—using the minimum number of constituent frequencies.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that only two harmonics are sufficient to generate superoscillations with a twofold local frequency enhancement, matching performance previously requiring four harmonics.
method: The analysis involves minimizing the combined electric field intensity over a time window and calculating the local frequency via Hilbert transformation.
model_or_system: The system is based on temporal domain optical superoscillations generated using quasi-sinusoidal THz harmonics, experimentally realized in Periodically Poled Lithium Niobate (PPLN).
key_observables: Local Frequency (floc), which quantifies the enhancement relative to the highest frequency component; signal amplitude.
important_parameters: Optimal frequency separation of approximately 10% is identified as a balance point between high local frequency enhancement and sufficient signal amplitude.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on modeling the combined field using sums of quasi-sinusoidal harmonics, and assumes that destructive interference can be controlled to enhance local oscillation rates.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the theoretical basis for bichromatic superoscillations. Figures 2 and 3 provide experimental confirmation (reanalyzed and new data) showing a clear twofold increase in local frequency using only two harmonics (e.g., 0.5/0.6 THz and 0.9/1 THz).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of superoscillation synthesis, presents the theoretical framework for bichromatic generation, provides analytical explanations regarding optimal frequency separation, and concludes with experimental validation using both reanalyzed historical data and new measurements.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced topics in quantum optics and light-matter interaction by demonstrating a significant technological simplification (reducing required harmonics from four to two) while maintaining high performance metrics relevant for super-sensing applications.
